findings.reasoning: Anyone can call PushBonusCode and add arbitrary values to the private bonusCodes array, allowing unauthorized users to manipulate contract state.
The function is public and lacks any authorization check, so any user can shrink the array and trigger the underflow bug.

When bonusCodes.length is zero, the statement `bonusCodes.length--` underflows to a very large value (pre‑0.8 Solidity), corrupting the array length and potentially causing out‑of‑gas or other failures.
No restriction on who can call UpdateBonusCodeAt, permitting any address to overwrite stored bonus codes.
